classification.difficultyReason: Move from a regular numerical case to an arbitrary star, recognise exterior angles counted twice across the tip triangles, and generalise that counting argument to n tips.

content.prompt: Investigate the outermost angles of stars formed by extending polygon sides.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The sides of a regular pentagon are extended to form a star. Find the measure of each of the outermost angles in this star.

spec.description: Regular five-point star with two upper tips, a horizontal segment joining the left and right tips, and one downward tip. Decorative cyan fill is omitted under house style.
spec.mathematics: Five intersecting straight segments enclose a regular central pentagon and five congruent tip triangles.
spec.answerVisibility: No answers or additional angle labels appear in the question figure.

answer.short:
$36^{\circ}$.

Each tip triangle has two base angles of $72^{\circ}$.
answer.worked:
Each interior angle of the regular pentagon is
$$\begin{align*}I&=\frac{(5-2)\times180^{\circ}}{5}\\I&=108^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
Each base angle of a tip triangle is $180^{\circ}-108^{\circ}=72^{\circ}$, using angles on a straight line. Therefore,
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^{\circ}-72^{\circ}-72^{\circ}\\\theta&=36^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: The sides of an arbitrary pentagon are extended to form a star. Find the sum of the outermost angles in this star.

spec.description: Irregular five-point star retaining its central pentagon, crossing incidences, horizontal lower-left to lower-right segment, upper-left and upper-right tips, and downward tip. Coordinates construct the illustration and are not numerical givens. Decorative cyan fill is omitted.
spec.mathematics: Five extended central-pentagon sides form five exterior tip triangles.
spec.answerVisibility: No supplied or derived angles appear in the question figure.

answer.short:
$180^{\circ}$.

The five tip triangles contain the pentagon’s exterior angles twice.
answer.worked:
Let $S$ be the sum of the five tip angles. The five tip triangles have a total angle sum of $5\times180^{\circ}$. Their ten base angles are the exterior angles of the central pentagon, each occurring twice. The exterior angles sum to $360^{\circ}$, so
$$\begin{align*}S&=5\times180^{\circ}-2\times360^{\circ}\\S&=180^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Suppose we extend the sides of an arbitrary $n$-gon to form a star with $n$ “points”. Find the sum of the outermost angles in this star.

answer.short:
$(n-4)\times180^{\circ}$, for the intended construction with one exterior tip triangle along each side.

Subtract twice the polygon’s exterior-angle sum from the angle sum of the $n$ tip triangles.
answer.worked:
For the intended construction, there are $n$ exterior tip triangles. Their base angles are the exterior angles of the central polygon, each occurring twice. Let $S$ be the sum of the tip angles. Then
$$\begin{align*}S&=n\times180^{\circ}-2\times360^{\circ}\\S&=(n-4)\times180^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
